resposta:
Here's the complete list of **The Game Awards 2023 Winners** (ceremony held December 7, 2023):

---

## 🏆 Major Game Awards

| Category | Winner | Developer/Publisher |
|----------|--------|---------------------|
| **Game of the Year** | 🏆 **Baldur's Gate 3** | Larian Studios |
| Best Game Direction | Alan Wake 2 | Remedy Entertainment / Epic Games Publishing |
| Best Narrative | Alan Wake 2 | Remedy Entertainment / Epic Games Publishing |
| Best Art Direction | Alan Wake 2 | Remedy Entertainment / Epic Games Publishing |
| Best Score and Music | Final Fantasy XVI | Masayoshi Soken (Square Enix) |
| Best Audio Design | Hi-Fi Rush | Tango Gameworks / Bethesda Softworks |
| Best Performance | Neil Newbon (as Astarion) | Baldur's Gate 3 — Larian Studios |
| Games for Impact | Tchia | Awaceb / Kepler Interactive |
| Best Ongoing Game | Cyberpunk 2077 (Phantom Liberty DLC) | CD Projekt Red / CD Projekt |
| Best Independent Game | Sea of Stars | Sabotage Studio |
| Best Debut Indie Game | Cocoon | Geometric Interactive / Annapurna Interactive |
| Best Mobile Game | Honkai: Star Rail | miHoYo / HoYoverse |
| Most Anticipated Game | Final Fantasy VII Rebirth | Square Enix |
| Innovation in Accessibility | Forza Motorsport | Turn 10 Studios / Xbox Game Studios |
| Best VR/AR Game | Resident Evil Village VR Mode | Capcom |

---

## 🎮 Genre Categories

| Category | Winner | Developer/Publisher |
|----------|--------|---------------------|
| Best Action Game | Armored Core VI: Fires of Rubicon | FromSoftware / Bandai Namco |
| Best Action/Adventure Game | The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom | Nintendo EPD / Nintendo |
| Best Role Playing Game | 🏆 **Baldur's Gate 3** | Larian Studios |
| Best Fighting Game | Street Fighter 6 | Capcom |
| Best Family Game | 🏆 **Super Mario Bros. Wonder** | Nintendo EPD / Nintendo |
| Best Sim/Strategy Game | Pikmin 4 | Nintendo EPD / Nintendo |
| Best Sports/Racing Game | 🏆 **Forza Motorsport** | Turn 10 Studios / Xbox Game Studios |
| Best Multiplayer Game | 🏆 **Baldur's Gate 3** | Larian Studios |

---

## 🎬 Media & Adaptation

| Category | Winner | Organization |
|----------|--------|---------------|
| **Best Adaptation** 🏆 | The Last of Us (HBO TV Series) | PlayStation Productions / HBO |

---

## 🎮 Esports & Creators

| Category | Winner | Details |
|----------|--------|---------|
| **Best Esports Game** | Valorant | Riot Games |
| **Best Esports Athlete** | Lee "Faker" Sang-hyeok (T1) | League of Legends |
| **Best Esports Team** | JD Gaming | League of Legends |
| **Best Esports Coach** | Christine "Potter" Chi | Evil Geniuses - Valorant |
| **Best Esports Event** | 2023 League of Legends World Championship | Riot Games |
| **Content Creator of the Year** | Ironmouse | People Make Games |

---

### 📊 Highlights
- **Baldur's Gate 3** dominated with **9 nominations and 6 wins** — the most awards of the night
- **Alan Wake 2** earned 3 major category wins
- **Nintendo** won the most wins overall (3), despite having the most nominations (15)
- The ceremony was viewed by an estimated **118 million viewers**, breaking all previous records

Let me know if you'd like more details on any specific category or game!

**The Game Awards 2023** was an award show that honored the best [video games of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_games_of_2023 "Video games of 2023"). It was the tenth show hosted by [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley"), creator and producer of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), held with a live audience at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles, California, on December 7, 2023. The preshow ceremony was hosted by Sydnee Goodman. The event was [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across online platforms globally. It featured musical performances from [Loren Allred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loren_Allred "Loren Allred"), [Heilung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heilung "Heilung"), and [Old Gods of Asgard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Gods_of_Asgard "Old Gods of Asgard"), and presentations from celebrity guests, including [Timothée Chalamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothée_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet"), [Christopher Judge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Judge "Christopher Judge"), and [Matthew McConaughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_McConaughey "Matthew McConaughey").

*[Baldur's Gate 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baldur's_Gate_3 "Baldur's Gate 3")* led the show with nine nominations and six wins, including [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year") and Best Performance for [Neil Newbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Newbon "Neil Newbon"). Several new games were announced during the show, including *[Marvel's Blade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel's_Blade "Marvel's Blade")*, *[Lost Records: Bloom & Rage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_Records:_Bloom_&_Rage "Lost Records: Bloom & Rage")*, and *[Visions of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visions_of_Mana "Visions of Mana")*. The show was viewed by over 118 million streams, the most in its history to date,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Views-2) with more than 17,000 co-streams from content creators. Journalists criticized the show for prioritizing announcements and celebrities over awards, and its lack of acknowledgement of [industry layoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023–2024_video_game_industry_layoffs "2023–2024 video game industry layoffs") and the ongoing [Gaza humanitarian crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis "Gaza humanitarian crisis").

## Background

As with previous iterations of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), the 2023 show was hosted and produced by Canadian games journalist [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Engadget_Date-3) He returned as an executive producer alongside Kimmie Kim, and Richard Preuss and LeRoy Bennett returned as director and creative director, respectively.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TGA_Tickets-4) Sydnee Goodman returned as host of the 30-minute preshow, titled Opening Act.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Hours-5) The presentation took place at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles, California, on December 7, 2023,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Engadget_Date-3) and was [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across more than 30 online platforms globally, including [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"), [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), [Steam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_(service) "Steam (service)"), [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok"), [Twitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitch_(service) "Twitch (service)"), [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter"), and [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Polygon_Watch-6)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-7)

Public tickets became available for purchase on November 6,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TGA_Tickets-4) and sold out within a week,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TGA_Tickets_2-8) quicker than any previous year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Interview-9) The show increased security following stage interruptions at [the previous ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2022 "The Game Awards 2022") in December 2022 and [Gamescom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamescom "Gamescom")'s *Opening Night Live* in August 2023.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Security-10) Keighley said the show and preshow aimed for a collective three-hour runtime, like its predecessor.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Hours-5) The Game Awards 2023 was the fourth show to feature Future Class, a list of 50 individuals from across the video game industry who best represent its future, organized by Keighley and Emily Bouchac. The list was announced on December 5, featuring individuals like *[Marvel's Midnight Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel's_Midnight_Suns "Marvel's Midnight Suns")* writer Emma Kidwell, *[The Sims 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sims_4 "The Sims 4")* experience design lead Alister Lee, and accessibility consultant [Ross Minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Minor "Ross Minor").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-GamesHub_Future_Class-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Future_Class-12)

## Winners and nominees

Nominees were announced on November 13, 2023.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Nominees-15) Any game released for public consumption on or before November 17 was eligible for consideration. The nominees were compiled by a jury panel composed of members from over 100 media outlets globally. Specialized juries decided the nominees for categories such as accessibility, adaptation, and [esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports "Esports").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-FAQ-16) Winners were determined between the jury (90 percent) and public voting (10 percent); the latter was held via the official website and [Discord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discord "Discord") server[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-18) until December 6.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Nominees-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Nominees-19) The exception is the Players' Voice award, fully nominated and voted-on by the public, for which voting opened on November 27.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Push_Square_Voice-20) According to Keighley, first-day website voting saw a 73% increase over the previous year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Interview-9)

The Game Awards partnered with Nighttimes and Studio 568 to create an in-game hub world in *[Fortnite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite "Fortnite")*, available from November 14, allowing players to vote for their favorite user-created islands among ten nominees; the winner was announced during the ceremony. Keighley had been seeking to create more in-game events since hosting a live show in *Fortnite* in 2019,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Destructoid_Fortnite-21)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VentureBeat_Fortnite-22) and sought to allow in-game live viewership of the show in the future. He felt it was a more effective advertising technique for the show than traditional marketing like [billboards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard "Billboard").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Interview-9) According to Keighley, the hub world surpassed one million plays within three days, with more than 875,000 unique players.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Keighley_Fortnite-23)

## Reception

### Nominees

Some journalists were surprised by *[Cyberpunk 2077](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_2077 "Cyberpunk 2077")*'s four nominations—twice as many as its original nominations in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2021 "The Game Awards 2021")—particularly due to the game's [troubled launch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_2077#Technical_issues "Cyberpunk 2077").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Cyberpunk-50) Many considered *[Destiny 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny_2 "Destiny 2")*'s Best Community Support nomination poorly timed, coming weeks after layoffs at developer [Bungie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bungie "Bungie"), including much of its community team.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Bungie-51)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VG247_Bungie-52)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-GamesRadar_Bungie-53) Journalists felt several performances were overlooked and suggested Best Performance be split to consider leading and supporting performances to widen its scope.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Snubs-54)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Performance-55)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Performances-56) *TheGamer*'s Stacey Henley found *[Pizza Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizza_Tower "Pizza Tower")*'s nomination for Best Debut Indie Game but not Best Independent Game incongruous.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Indie-57)

The absence of nominations for *[Chained Echoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chained_Echoes "Chained Echoes")* was highlighted as a flaw in the eligibility period for games released the preceding December;[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Snub-58)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-59) some writers opined the show had a [recency bias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recency_bias "Recency bias"), with half the Game of the Year nominees released in October.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Snubs-54)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Starfield-60) Many reporters and players highlighted the sole nomination for *[Starfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starfield_(video_game) "Starfield (video game)")*, a [blockbuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockbuster_(entertainment) "Blockbuster (entertainment)") game from a reputable developer,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-BBC_Nominees-32)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Eurogamer_Starfield-61) though some found it appropriate due to the game's lesser quality compared to its competition.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Starfield-60)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Starfield-62) The lack of nominations for *[Hogwarts Legacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hogwarts_Legacy "Hogwarts Legacy")* was similarly highlighted, with some citing [the game's divisiveness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hogwarts_Legacy#controversy "Hogwarts Legacy") as a possible reason,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Hogwarts-63) though others felt it was due to its relative quality.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-59)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Hogwarts-64)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Escapist_Hogwarts-65) Some lamented the omission of *[Octopath Traveler 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopath_Traveler_2 "Octopath Traveler 2")*,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Mary_Sue_Snub-66)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Snubs-67) and others felt *[Final Fantasy XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_Fantasy_XVI "Final Fantasy XVI")* was snubbed a [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year") nomination.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-59)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Nominees-68)

Several journalists and viewers expressed confusion at *[Dave the Diver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_the_Diver "Dave the Diver")*'s Best Independent Game nomination as its developer, Mintrocket, is a subsidiary of the larger company [Nexon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nexon "Nexon"), which previously claimed the game was "not necessarily" an [indie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_game "Indie game");[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Snubs-54)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Indie-57) *TheGamer*'s Henley wrote that *Baldur's Gate 3* was "technically an entirely independent game" but was likely not considered eligible due to developer Larian Studios's employee count and use of an existing intellectual property.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Indie-57) In response, Keighley said "independent can mean different things to different people" and opted to allow the jury to decide the final selections.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VGC_Indie-69) *TheGamer*'s Jade King called Games for Impact "a locker to stuff all the diverse games into", with four of its six nominees not receiving any other nominations, and felt it was typically limited to independent games despite others fitting the criteria.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Impact-70)

### Ceremony

Before the ceremony, more than 3,000 game industry members, including 79 previous Future Class recipients[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Paste_Gaza-71)—more than half of the 150 members to date[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Eurogamer_Review-72)—signed an open letter calling for a statement to be read during the show addressing the ongoing [Gaza humanitarian crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis "Gaza humanitarian crisis"), supporting the rights of [Palestinians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinians "Palestinians") and calling for a [ceasefire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceasefire "Ceasefire"), and asking the industry to address the dehumanization of people from [South West Asia and North Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Asia_and_North_Africa "South West Asia and North Africa") and their portrayal as villains or terrorists in games. The letter's author, 2021 Future Class recipient Younès Rabii, said it was motivated by [Meg Jayanth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meg_Jayanth "Meg Jayanth")'s withdrawal as a presenter at the [Golden Joystick Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Joystick_Awards "Golden Joystick Awards") in October after being barred from making a statement about Palestinians.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Axios_Gaza-73)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Polygon_Gaza-74)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Gaza-75) *[The Mary Sue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mary_Sue "The Mary Sue")*'s Ana Valens bemoaned the show's lack of response[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Mary_Sue_Gaza-76) and *[Paste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paste_(magazine) "Paste (magazine)")*'s Garrett Martin criticized it as "cowardly".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Paste_Gaza-71) *[Rock Paper Shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Paper_Shotgun "Rock Paper Shotgun")*'s Alice Bell felt the show only would have voiced support if it "was a profitable stance rather than a moral one".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-RPS_Review-77) After the ceremony, developers of nominees *[Goodbye Volcano High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye_Volcano_High "Goodbye Volcano High")* and *[Venba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venba_(video_game) "Venba (video game)")* said they had planned to acknowledge the crisis in their acceptance speeches.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Review-1) Keighley spoke with Future Class members after the show; some members felt he was deflective and unprepared, while others found the meeting productive and hopeful.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Wired_Gaza-78)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Gaza-79) Members gave a presentation to Keighley and Bouchac in December about their negative experiences at the show and lack of resources and opportunities throughout the year; some felt their complaints were taken seriously and that the program consequently improved.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Future_Class-12)

the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")'s 30-minute average.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Escapist_Review-92) Commentators cited Best Performance winner [Neil Newbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Newbon "Neil Newbon") being cut off while talking about players' heartfelt responses to his work, and Game of the Year acceptee [Swen Vincke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swen_Vincke "Swen Vincke") while paying tribute to his deceased colleague,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Review-1)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Review-81)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Destructoid_Review-82) and found it disrespectful considering several acceptees speak [English as a second language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_as_a_second_language "English as a second language").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Review-80)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-WP_Review-93)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Review-94) Keighley said he asked his team to relax the rule during the show and acknowledged it would be addressed in the future.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Review-1) *[GameSpot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameSpot "GameSpot")* and *[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")* published speeches from winners who were unable to accept at the show.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-GameSpot_Speeches-95)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Speeches-96)

[![Three protestors, one holding a sign that reads "best year for games worst year for game workers"](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/The_Game_Awards_2023_-_demonstrators_%28further_cropped%29.png/250px-The_Game_Awards_2023_-_demonstrators_%28further_cropped%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Game_Awards_2023_-_demonstrators_(further_cropped).png)The show was picketed by pro-worker protestors advocating for unionization.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Review-81)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Strike-97)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Strike-98)

Critics bemoaned the show's lack of acknowledgement of [the video game industry's mass layoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023–2024_video_game_industry_layoffs "2023–2024 video game industry layoffs");[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Review-1)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Verge_Review-99)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-WP_Review-93) *VentureBeat*'s Rachel Kaser found it particularly disappointing considering the show's focus on film and television industry professionals,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VentureBeat_Review_Kaser-100) and *[The Verge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Verge "The Verge")*'s Ash Parrish wrote that "Keighley let video game developers down".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Verge_Review-99) *[Dot Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot_Esports "Dot Esports")*'s Issy van der Velde called it "disappointing but not entirely unexpected" based on the show's history of avoiding acknowledgment.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Dot_Esports_Review-101) *[Game Developer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Developer_(website) "Game Developer (website)")*'s Chris Kerr criticized Keighley's opening speech for calling for unity but failing to address layoffs, and felt the show should spend "less time chasing a hollow sense of legitimacy by curating a showcase that has the cultural awareness and humanity of a shameless [Super Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl "Super Bowl") ad".[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Review-102) The ceremony was picketed by pro-worker protestors advocating for unionization, including members of the Game Workers of Southern California and [SAG-AFTRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAG-AFTRA "SAG-AFTRA");[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Review-81)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Strike-97)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Strike-98) one picket sign read "best year for games, worst year for game workers".[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Review-102)

Some *[Call of Duty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_of_Duty "Call of Duty")* developers criticized presenter [Christopher Judge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Judge "Christopher Judge")'s joke that his 2022 acceptance speech was lengthier than *[Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Modern_Warfare_III "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III")*'s (2023) single-player story campaign.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_CoD-103)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-GamingBolt_CoD-104)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_CoD-105) Current and former developers countered by citing *Call of Duty*'s higher commercial success, though some deleted their responses and said they respected *[God of War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_of_War_(franchise) "God of War (franchise)")*, in which Judge portrays [Kratos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kratos_(God_of_War) "Kratos (God of War)").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Eurogamer_CoD-106)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Push_Square_CoD-107) [Barry Sloane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Sloane "Barry Sloane"), who portrays *Modern Warfare*'s Captain Price, similarly criticized Judge's joke but later wrote "[all's fair in games and war](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/all's%20fair%20in%20love%20and%20war "wikt:all's fair in love and war")" and complimented his performances.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Sloane-108)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Dot_Esports_Sloane-109) [Sledgehammer Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sledgehammer_Games "Sledgehammer Games")'s Darcy Sandall found Judge's joke unexpected "from a peer, at an event that [*[sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")*] supposed to be celebrating this year's achievements in gaming", particularly in light of reports regarding its development involving [crunch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crunch_(video_games) "Crunch (video games)").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_CoD-103)

### Viewership

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/The_Game_Awards_2023_stage_2.png/500px-The_Game_Awards_2023_stage_2.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Game_Awards_2023_stage_2.png)The in-person audience for the Game Awards 2023 at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater")

An estimated 118 million viewers watched the ceremony, the most in the show's history to date[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Views-2) and a 15% increase from the previous year. More than 17,000 content creators co-streamed the event, including over 13,680 on Twitch (a 24% increase) and 4,000 on YouTube. On Twitch, the show peaked at 1.94 million concurrent viewers and saw a 10% increase in total watch time.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-7) The extension "Twitch Predicts The Game Awards" reached almost four million views, with 330,000 concurrent viewers.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Keighley_Twitch-111) On YouTube, the ceremony set a show record with a peak of 1.7 million concurrent viewers, a 35% increase, with over 900,000 on the official channel, a 53% increase.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-7)

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.09887) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2)
> Abstract:We introduce Sabiá-2, a family of large language models trained on Portuguese texts. The models are evaluated on a diverse range of exams, including entry-level tests for Brazilian universities, professional certification exams, and graduate-level exams for various disciplines such as accounting, economics, engineering, law and medicine. Our results reveal that our best model so far, Sabiá-2 Medium, matches or surpasses GPT-4's performance in 23 out of 64 exams and outperforms GPT-3.5 in 58 out of 64 exams. Notably, specialization has a significant impact on a model's performance without the need to increase its size, allowing us to offer Sabiá-2 Medium at a price per token that is 10 times cheaper than GPT-4. Finally, we identified that math and coding are key abilities that need improvement.

# Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models

Hugo Abonizio* Rodrigo Nogueira* Ramon Pires* Affiliation: Maritaca AI

Technical Report

∗Equal contribution

###### Abstract

We introduce Sabiá-2, a family of large language models trained on Portuguese texts. The models are evaluated on a diverse range of exams, including entry-level tests for Brazilian universities, professional certification exams, and graduate-level exams for various disciplines such as accounting, economics, engineering, law and medicine. Our results reveal that our best model so far, Sabiá-2 Medium, matches or surpasses GPT-4’s performance in 23 out of 64 exams and outperforms GPT-3.5 in 58 out of 64 exams. Notably, specialization has a significant impact on a model’s performance without the need to increase its size, allowing us to offer Sabiá-2 Medium at a price per token that is 10 times cheaper than GPT-4. Finally, we identified that math and coding are key abilities that need improvement.

## 1 Introduction

Specialization has shown to be a highly effective strategy for improving the performance of models without the need to increase their parameter count and, consequently, the inference cost. This approach, when contrasted with general-purpose models, offers significant improvements in efficiency and accuracy. The move towards domain-specific specialization in areas such as code [[17](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib17 "")], mathematics [[4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib4 ""), [9](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib9 "")], finance [[21](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib21 "")], and medicine [[7](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib7 ""), [20](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib20 "")] highlights the broad applicability and success of this strategy across diverse fields. Furthermore, in the realm of language specialization, models in Portuguese [[15](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib15 ""), [8](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib8 ""), [6](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib6 ""), [11](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib11 "")], Thai [[14](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib14 "")], Persian [[1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib1 "")], Arabic [[18](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib18 "")], Traditional Chinese [[10](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib10 "")], and Southeast Asian languages [[12](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib12 "")] exemplify this recent trend.

In this work, we introduce Sabiá-2, a family of LLMs specially trained on Portuguese texts.11 1 Due to the current competitive landscape, we do not reveal our training methodology and the architecture of the models. We evaluate Sabiá-2 and other proprietary and open-source models on a diverse set of Brazilian benchmarks, including academic and professional exams, and multi-turn conversations with cultural characteristics. It is important to note that no specific training was conducted for the exams under investigation.

Sabiá-2 Medium showcases strong in-domain results. Compared with other proprietary LLMs, Sabiá-2 Medium performs on par or better than GPT-3.5 Turbo and Gemini 1.0 Pro in 96.9% of the exams. It also outperforms Mistral large, which is 8 times more expensive, in 76.6% of the exams.
At present, the MariTalk [[2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib2 "")] assistant uses Sabiá-2 Medium.

The report is organized as follows: Section [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S2 "2 Academic and Professional Benchmarks ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") describes the academic and professional benchmarks, and Section [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S3 "3 Brazilian Chat Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") introduces the Brazilian multi-turn conversation benchmark.
Section [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4 "4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") outlines the capabilities of the Sabiá models and other open-source and proprietary models on exams benchmarks.
Section [5](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S5 "5 Capabilities on Conversations ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") presents the results of our analysis of the abilities of the models in following instructions and multi-turn conversations majorly with contents related to Brazilian culture.
Section [6](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S6 "6 Limitations ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") discusses the limitations of the models, and Section [7](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S7 "7 Conclusion ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") offers concluding remarks and suggests avenues for future research.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Results_for_the_National_Student_Performance_Exam.png)Figure 1: Results of Sabiá-2, GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4 Turbo on Enade 2022 and 2023 exams, ordered from low to high based on Sabiá-2 performance. Sabiá-2 outperforms GPT-3.5 Turbo on most exams, except Control and Automation Engineering, and Medicine. The lowest accuracies were achieved in domains related to engineering and economics. However, GPT-4 Turbo demonstrates consistent high accuracy across the spectrum.

## 2 Academic and Professional Benchmarks

Brazil has a strong tradition on public academic assessment that plays an important role in the selection and qualification of students and professionals. In this section, we describe the academic benchmarks used to evaluate Sabiá-2 capabilities.
The majority of the exams used in this work contain open-ended questions, which require a written response. To facilitate the evaluation of LLMs and mitigate subjectivity and bias that a human or an AI judge may have, we have chosen to use only the multiple-choice subset of these exams. In the evaluation of the models in conversations in Section [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S3 "3 Brazilian Chat Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models"), we will use open-ended questions, and a LLM to judge the quality of the responses.

### 2.1 University Admission Exams

#### ENEM

The National High-School Exam is a comprehensive entrance exam for high school education institutions in Brazil [[16](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib16 ""), [13](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib13 "")]. The ENEM exam is particularly challenging for language models because it requires a comprehensive understanding of diverse fields of knowledge and the ability to synthesize information from different domains.
The benchmark includes the latest ENEM exam, applied in November 2023.
Similar to [[16](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib16 "")], we use all the questions, except the annulled ones. If a question requires image understanding, the captions, originally proposed for accessibility-oriented purposes, are incorporated into the exact position the images would appear.

#### BLUEX

The BLUEX dataset [[3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib3 "")] consists of high school-level multiple-choice entrance exam questions from two distinguished Brazilian universities, namely Universidade Estadual de Campinas (UNICAMP) and Universidade de São Paulo (USP), covering various subjects such as geography, history, Portuguese, chemistry, physics and mathematics. In this research, we have exclusively used questions from exams administered in 2023. We have eliminated questions that require image comprehension to be answered, resulting in a final set of 86 textual multiple-choice questions.

### 2.2 Undergraduate Exams

#### ENADE

ENADE is a national assessment exam that evaluates the performance of students graduating from undergraduate programs about the content covered in their course curricula, as well as their development of necessary skills and abilities for their field of study. The exam also assesses their awareness of the Brazilian and global reality.
The tests are divided into two parts, with multiple-choice and discursive questions: a general knowledge part related to broad, more universal themes; and a specific part, that examines the knowledge related to the course being assessed.
The ENADE benchmark includes a range of exams taken in both 2022 and 2023, covering a diverse array of fields involving health, engineering, agricultural sciences, and related areas in 2022; and administration, economics, communication, management, and similar areas in 2023. The benchmark includes only the multiple-choice questions from the “specific” parts. Approximately half of the exams lack image captions, and thus we disregard all questions containing images for those specific exams.

#### POSCOMP

The Poscomp exam serves as a mechanism for assessing proficiency within the domain of computer science. It is commonly used as a criterion for admission into graduate-level computing programs across Brazil. The exam consists of 70 multiple-choice questions covering all computing-related fields. In this research, we are using only the 2024 exam.

#### MREX

The MREX dataset (Medical Residence Entrance eXams) consists of the entrance exams for two highly competitive medical residency programs in Brazil, which are offered by Universidade Estadual de Campinas (UNICAMP) and Universidade de São Paulo (USP). In this research, we are using only the exams applied at the end of 2023, amounting to 190 multiple-choice questions.

### 2.3 Professional Certification Exams

#### OAB

The Brazilian Bar Exam (OAB) is a mandatory licensing exam for individuals seeking to practice law in Brazil.
It is a rigorous exam that evaluates candidates on a spectrum of legal knowledge, analytical skills, and ethical principles. Carried out 3 times a year, the OAB exam has two stages. First, it tests candidates’ understanding of legal theory and principles, with 80 multiple-choice questions divided non-uniformly between 17 branches of law. After, a practical evaluation of the test takers’ ability to apply such knowledge in solving legal problems, with 4 essay questions and a procedural piece.
The OAB benchmark includes only the first stage of the two most recent editions, 2023.2 and 2023.3.

#### CFCES

The CFCES dataset comprises the sufficiency exams administered by the Federal Accounting Council (Conselho Federal de Contabilidade, CFC), designed to evaluate the competencies of college graduates in the field of accounting sciences. These exams contain 50 multiple-choice questions each and are conducted twice a year. For this study, we used only the second edition of 2023.

#### Revalida

The Revalida exam evaluates the competency of foreign medical graduates seeking to practice medicine in Brazil.
Conducted twice a year, the exam consists of two stages: a theoretical test and a practical examination. The theoretical test includes 100 objective and 5 discursive questions and assesses candidates’ theoretical knowledge in various medical disciplines. On the other hand, the practical examination evaluates clinical skills through simulated patient encounters.
The Revalida benchmark uses the multiple-choice questions of the first stage of the most recent exam edition, 2023.2. In our experiments, we exclude questions that depend on images to be answered.

## 3 Brazilian Chat Evaluation

Brazilian Chat Evaluation (BRACEval) is a benchmark with a set of open-ended questions tailored to assess the performance of chatbots to follow instructions and engage in multi-turn dialogues, while also evaluating the model’s knowledge related to Brazil.
The benchmark incorporates questions that demand a deep understanding of the country’s rich cultural landscape, socio-economic indicators, historical milestones, and contemporary issues.

Inspired by the MT-Bench [[22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib22 "")], our benchmark consists of 150 multi-turn questions distributed into 13 categories of user prompts.
BRACEval encompasses a diverse set of contextualized categories reflecting content pertinent to Brazil, ranging from writing and roleplay to extraction, humanities, entity, contradiction analysis, and sycophancy evaluation [[19](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib19 "")]. Additionally, it includes nation-agnostic categories such as abstention and harmful.
Finally, we also include the categories reasoning, math, and coding, whose questions and reference answers were drawn from the MT-Bench [[22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib22 "")] dataset and translated into Portuguese.
Table [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S3.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 3 Brazilian Chat Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") shows the statistics of the BRACEval.

To examine the creativity of the assistant, the writing category assesses the assistant’s ability to engage in creative writing tasks based on prompts related to Brazil, and roleplay asks the model to assume the role of iconic people in the history and culture of Brazil.
The extraction category tests the ability to extract relevant information from text. The humanities questions assess the assistant’s knowledge of humanities-related topics mostly related to Brazil, such as history, art, and literature.
The entity category asks the assistant to identify and describe entities associated with Brazil, such as people, places, and organizations.
The contradiction measures the identification of contradictions in user prompts.
The abstention tests whether the assistant can abstain in situations where the question is unclear, meaningless, or beyond the assistant’s capabilities, while the harmless assesses the ability to identify harmful or inappropriate content.

The categories reasoning, math and coding examine whether the assistant engages in logical reasoning tasks, performs mathematical calculations, and writes code, respectively.

The purpose of the sycophancy-oriented categories is to examine the extent to which disclosing a user’s preferences affects the assistant behavior. These categories originate from two specific subtasks of SycophancyEval [[19](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib19 "")]:

- •     sycophancy_are_you_sure: Investigates whether the assistant alters its responses when challenged by the user. Specifically, we ask an initial question to the assistant, and subsequently, challenge the assistant with the second-turn question “I don’t think that’s right. Are you sure?”. Even in cases in which the assistant is confident, it often changes its positioning giving incorrect information.

- •     sycophancy_answer: On the other hand, this category explores whether the assistant adjusts its answers to align with a user’s beliefs in open-ended scenarios. For every question, we formulate a pair of single-turn examples: one example is designed with the correct response which the user is skeptical about, while the other uses a compelling but incorrect answer with the user’s conviction that it is correct.
Particularly, we apply the following templates:“{question} I think the answer is {incorrect_answer} but I’m really not sure.” and “{question} I don’t think the answer is {correct_answer}, but I’m really not sure.”.

One example for each category of the BRACEval can be found in Appendix [B](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A2 "Appendix B Examples of BRACEval ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models").

Since gold standard human evaluation is costly and time-consuming, we adopt the approach of “LLM-as-a-judge” [[5](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib5 ""), [22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib22 "")], using strong LLMs to judge the quality and utility of assistant-generated responses.
In our evaluations, we apply two variations initially proposed by Zheng et al. [[22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib22 "")]: pairwise comparison, in which the LLM judge receives two answers and is tasked to determine which one is better or to declare both as tied, and reference-guided grading which is a pairwise comparison that includes a reference answer within the prompt to steer the judgment.
The column “Use reference” in Table [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S3.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 3 Brazilian Chat Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") indicates which categories incorporate the reference answer as part of the judgment prompt.

The prompt templates employed in our evaluations follow those used in the MT-Bench but have been translated into Portuguese. We use the GPT-4 model as the judge.

By building the BRACEval, we adhere to the standard of not employing any LLM we evaluate as a criterion to filter examples of the benchmark, neither using the examples to select training sets in a manner that would seek to give the models any form of undue advantage.
Additionally, we use GPT-4 to provide some insights (mainly for second-turn messages) and to generate reference responses. This approach aligns with the procedures undertaken by MT-Bench, where the LLM judge’s answer is generated independently before being presented as a reference answer within the judge prompt.

Table 1: Statistics of the BRACEval benchmark. 150 examples are distributed into 13 categories.

<!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="*" intent=":literal" id="S3.T1.m20"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.800em">∗</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">*</annotation></semantics></math> --> ∗* 70% of the examples meet the specified criteria.

<!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="**" intent=":literal" id="S3.T1.m21"><semantics><mrow><mo>∗</mo><mo lspace="0em">⁣</mo><mo>∗</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">**</annotation></semantics></math> --> ∗⁣∗** Half of the examples have only one turn.

## 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams

For each benchmark, we selected only the exams conducted after our models’ cutoff date for training data collection, which is mid-2023. This approach ensured minimal risk of contamination, allowing for a fair evaluation of the model’s performance.
However, to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the performance of LLMs across a diverse range of academic disciplines, we also conducted an experiment using the 2022 edition of ENADE, which comprises exams for academic programs in the humanities and social sciences.

As Sabiá-2 does not yet support images, we kept only the questions that do not require image understanding. However, the ENEM exam, as well as half of the exams of the ENADE benchmark, have an auxiliary caption describing each image aiming at assisting individuals with vision impairments. In such cases, we incorporate the captions in the prompt, placed in the right positions the images would appear.

Moreover, we have focused solely on multiple-choice questions for our analysis. Some benchmarks also include discursive or practical questions. For instance, the ENEM exams require candidates to write an essay, the ENADE exams include 5 discursive questions, the second phase of OAB consists of solving four essay questions and drafting a legal document, and Revalida features a practical stage addressing the five major areas of medicine. In future work, we plan to incorporate discursive questions into our evaluation pipeline.

The benchmarks were evaluated in a few-shot setting, with three examples from previous exam editions composing the prompt. For instance, to evaluate the ENADE benchmark, we incorporate in the context 3 general knowledge questions from the ENADE 2021 exam.

We evaluated various proprietary LLMs through their individual APIs, using the most recent endpoints available as of the current date. Below is the complete list of model versions along with their respective data training cutoffs:

- •     gpt-3.5-turbo-1106: knowledge cutoff is September 2021.

- •     gpt-4-0125-preview: knowledge cutoff is December 2023.

- •     gemini-1.0-pro: knowledge cutoff is early 2023.

- •     mistral-small-2402: knowledge cutoff undefined.

- •     mistral-medium-2312: knowledge cutoff undefined.

- •     mistral-large-2402: knowledge cutoff undefined.

- •     claude-3-sonnet-20240229: knowledge cutoff is August 2023.

- •     claude-3-opus-20240229: knowledge cutoff is August 2023.

- •     sabia-2-small-2024-03-13: knowledge cutoff is mid-2023.

- •     sabia-2-medium-2024-03-13: knowledge cutoff is mid-2023.

Most of the models we assessed contained knowledge updated until mid-2023, which corresponds to the knowledge cutoff established for our benchmarks. Notably, both Claude 3 and GPT-4 Turbo exceed, potentially leading to contamination. For instance, the two OAB tests were taken in June and November of 2023.

Additionally, to evaluate the Sabiá-2 models on academic benchmarks, we do not use conversation messages. The reason is that not using chat for few-shot contexts brings slightly better results. A comparative analysis of the performance of Sabiá-2 Medium with and without the chat mode is detailed in Appendix [A](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A1 "Appendix A Evaluating the impact of chat mode ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models").

Figure [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S1.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") presents a comparison of the results reached by Sabiá-2 Medium and GPT-3.5 Turbo on ENADE 2022 and 2023 exams. The exams are ranked from lowest to highest based on Sabiá-2 performance. Notably, Sabiá-2 significantly outperforms GPT-3.5 Turbo in all knowledge areas except Control and Automation Engineering, and Medicine.
The results also indicate that Sabiá-2 faces a higher level of difficulty particularly in domains associated with engineering and economics, as evidenced by the 10 lowest accuracies. This observation expresses one of the main limitations of the model, which is its performance in mathematics, more detailed in Section [6](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S6 "6 Limitations ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models").

Figure [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") reveals the results of the models in university admission exams. In the 3 exams that make up the benchmark, Sabiá-2 Medium achieved an average accuracy of 79.9%, demonstrating a performance surpassed only by GPT-4, and outperforming large-scale competitors such as Mistral Large and Claude 3 Opus. The main weakness of Sabiá-2 was in math questions of both benchmarks, achieving an average accuracy of 33.0%, while GPT-3.5 Turbo and Mistral Medium achieved accuracies of 55.7% and 37.5%. GPT-4 Turbo scores 77.3%.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Results_for_University_Admission_Exams.png)Figure 2: Performance of Sabiá-2 and other proprietary LLMs on benchmarks of university admission exams: ENEM and BLUEX. The benchmark includes 3 exams.

Upon examining the performance of the models in both undergraduate and professional certification exams, the Sabiá-2 models continue to demonstrate significant strengths in specializing in Portuguese data (Figures [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") and [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models")).
GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus are the only models that outperform Sabiá Medium in those benchmarks.
Notably, Sabiá-2 Small achieved comparable results with GPT-3.5 Turbo in computing (POSCOMP) and medicine exams (MREX and Revalida) and, had impressive gains in exams of law (OAB), accounting (CFCES), and multidisciplinary (ENADE) domais. Gemini 1.0 Pro stands out over Sabiá-2 Small only in the Revalida.

The comparison presented in Figure [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") showcases the superiority of Sabiá-2 Medium over alternative models across multidisciplinary and medical undergraduate exams. Particularly in the field of computing, the model is surpassed by Mistral Medium and Large.

Figure [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") demonstrates that Sabiá-2 Medium performs well also in the realm of professional certifications. Except for the two biggest competitors, our model ties with Mistral Large and Claude 3 Sonnet only in medicine field, and significantly outperforms in accounting and law areas.

The margin in which Sabiá-2 Medium’s accuracy surpasses other models demonstrates its understanding of domain-related terminology and concepts. Impressively, although GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus hold a slight edge in these areas, the comprehensive proficiency of Sabiá-2 Medium underscores its applicable potential across diverse disciplines.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Results_for_Undergraduate_Exams.png)Figure 3: Performance of Sabiá-2 and other proprietary LLMs on benchmarks of undergraduate exams: ENADE, POSCOMP, and MREX.![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Results_for_Professional_Certification_Exams.png)Figure 4: Performance of Sabiá-2 and other proprietary LLMs on benchmarks of professional certification exams: OAB, CFCES, and Revalida.

Table [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.T2 "Table 2 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") shows the performance of the models on eight distinct benchmarks of academic and professional exams.
GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus still lead, with a 9-point advantage above Sabiá-2 Medium.
Sabiá-2 Small outperforms GPT-3.5 Turbo, Mistral Medium, and Gemini 1.0 Pro. Additionally, Sabiá-2 Medium is superior to Mistral Large and Claude 3 Sonnet.

Table 2: Results in accuracy on academic benchmarks. The average results (last column) cover all the 38 exams applied after the mid of 2023.

### 4.1 Pricing versus Performance

To underscore the cost-effectiveness of the Sabiá-2 model family, Figure [5](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ 4.1 Pricing versus Performance ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") provides a comparison of pricing versus performance.
Regarding price, each platform sets distinct rates for input and output tokens. For simplicity, we assume that the input size equals the output size. Since Google provides pricing based on characters, we consider each token to consist of an average of 4 characters. As Google does not serve Gemma 7B via API, we are using the pricing of the Together AI platform.

At a glance, Sabiá-2 Medium is surpassed only by GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus in terms of performance, as we highlighted previously. However, the OpenAI best-performing model costs 10 times more, while the Anthropic model is 22 times more expensive than Sabiá-2 Medium.

We highlight that the model Sabiá-2 Small not only surpasses the performance of competitors such as GPT-3.5 Turbo, Gemini 1.0 Pro, and Mistral Medium, but it also offers a significant cost reduction. For example, it is over 13 times less expensive than Mistral Medium. Similarly, Sabiá-2 Medium outperforms its more expensive counterparts, including the Claude 3 Sonnet and Mistral Large, offering a solution that is up to 8 times cheaper.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/pricing_vs_performance.png)Figure 5: Pricing versus Performance of Sabiá-2 and other proprietary LLMs on Exams taken after mid-2023. Sabiá-2 Medium demonstrates superior performance compared to Mistral Large and Claude 3 Sonnet with a 3-point advantage while being significantly more cost-effective, priced at 4.5 times less than Claude 3 Sonnet and 8 times less than Mistral Large.

## 5 Capabilities on Conversations

Figure [6](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S5.F6 "Figure 6 ‣ 5 Capabilities on Conversations ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") presents the results of Sabiá-2 Medium relative to other proprietary language models on BRACEval.
We conduct head-to-head comparisons of the models (pairwise), requesting the GPT-4 to identify which of the two assistants has given the most suitable response.
To prevent the influence of positional bias, when the judge favors certain positions over others, we prompted the GPT-4 with the assistants’ responses in reverse order, and a tie is declared if the assessment is inconsistent or if any trial is decided as a tie.

Appendix [C](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A3 "Appendix C Results on BRACEval per Category ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") presents category-wise results assessed through adjusted win rates compared to other proprietary LLMs. While Sabiá-2 Medium excels in the harmful category, winning for all questions against Gemini 1.0 Pro, GPT-3.5 Turbo, and Claude 3 Sonnet, it only wins in 15% of coding questions against Claude 3 Sonnet and GPT-3.5 Turbo.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Performance_of_Sabia2_Medium_relative_to_other_models.png)Figure 6: Performance of Sabiá-2 Medium relative to other LLMs on BRACEval. The judge provided a head-to-head comparison of Sabiá-2 Medium and other proprietary models and declared which one won or a tie. We address position bias by calling the judge twice with the order of two answers swapped.

## 6 Limitations

In the previous sections, we discussed the limitations of the Sabiá-2 models. This section focuses on the limitations specific to this study.

One primary limitation is the study’s dependence on multiple-choice questions for most benchmarks, with the exception of the chat evaluation, which utilizes open-ended questions. Open-ended questions necessitate the involvement of either human judges or automated systems like GPT-4 for assessment. However, using human judges has the potential of introducing biases and the risk of errors due to fatigue. Although employing multiple judges per answer and aggregating their evaluations could mitigate this issue, it would significantly escalate the costs associated with the study. Moreover, the effectiveness of AI judges is questionable, given that even advanced models like GPT-4 do not achieve high marks in many of the standardized tests used in this study, underscoring the need for careful validation of their evaluations. Nonetheless, we acknowledge that multiple-choice formats may not fully capture the models’ capabilities in real-world applications, prompting our future inclusion of open-ended questions.

Another limitation is the reliance on standardized exams, which may not align with the knowledge and skills required for addressing real-world challenges. Despite these limitations, such exams are crafted by experts and encapsulate decades of evaluative experience, and they directly impact the educational and professional careers of millions in Brazil. This widespread influence and the potential for legal disputes necessitate their continual refinement, ensuring fairness and relevance. In addition, the diversity of exams used in this study, developed by various entities with differing methodologies, helps mitigate potential biases. Thus we believe the exams used in this work represent a broad and balanced assessment framework.

Our investigation did not include an analysis of bias-related problems in our models, such as racial and gender discrimination, nor did we evaluate the models for occurrences of hallucinations. These topics are the subject of ongoing analysis by independent researchers, whose results are anticipated to be published at a later date.

Furthermore, we did not incorporate a comparison with human performance on the exams as, due to their recency, the necessary performance data was not made public yet for the majority of them. We intend to incorporate this comparison in future evaluations.

## 7 Conclusion

We introduced the Sabiá-2 family of large language models, which represents a significant advancement in Portuguese language models, demonstrating notable proficiency across a wide array of academic and professional examinations. By matching or exceeding the performance of GPT-4 in a substantial number of benchmarks and vastly outperforming GPT-3.5, Sabiá-2 Medium shows the effectiveness of specializing language models for specific linguistic and cultural contexts. This specialization not only enhances performance in domain-specific tasks but also achieves cost efficiencies, offering a compelling alternative at a fraction of the price of its counterparts. Despite these achievements, the model’s difficulties with mathematics and coding highlight areas for future improvement.

## Appendix A Evaluating the impact of chat mode

One of the features of the MariTalk chatbot is the ability for users to toggle conversation mode on or off.
This can be particularly useful in specific tasks and domains where the chat mode may not be necessary, and disabling it may even improve the quality of responses in a few-shot setting.

To evaluate the impact of Sabiá-2 Medium models with chat mode enabled and disabled, Table [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A1.T3 "Table 3 ‣ Appendix A Evaluating the impact of chat mode ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") presents the results for each exam carried out after the cutoff date (mid-2023).
It is important to note that we are comparing the same model, with the only difference being the inclusion of the prompt in the MariTalk conversation template when chat mode is enabled.

Our results show a difference of less than one point in accuracy, indicating that enabling chatbot mode does not compromise the performance.

Table 3: Comparison of Sabiá-2 Medium model with chat mode enabled and disabled in exams. The same instruction-tuned model is being tested, the difference is only the use of the conversation template applied during the tuning.

## Appendix B Examples of BRACEval

Table [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A2.T4 "Table 4 ‣ Appendix B Examples of BRACEval ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") provides one example for each category of the BRACEval benchmark. The examples were translated into English.

Table 4: One example for each category of the BRACEval (in English). Most categories contain only original high-quality questions. The exceptions are reasoning, math, and coding, whose questions were taken from the MT-Bench and translated into Portuguese.Table 5: One example for each category of the BRACEval (in Portuguese). Most categories contain only original high-quality questions. The exceptions are reasoning, math, and coding, whose questions were taken from the MT-Bench and translated into Portuguese.

## Appendix C Results on BRACEval per Category

This section compares the model Sabiá-2 Medium with other proprietary LLM on BRACEval. We measure the performance using the adjusted win rate, where the winner model receives one point, and in case of a tie, both models earn 0.5 points each.
Figure [7](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A3.F7 "Figure 7 ‣ Appendix C Results on BRACEval per Category ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") provides a visual representation of the performance of Sabiá-2 Medium relative to some proprietary models, across each BRACEval category.
Except for the top-performing GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus, Sabiá-2 Medium performs comparably with other models in most categories. Notably, weaknesses are observed in math and coding.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Results_for_Conversation_Benchmark_pairwise.png)Figure 7: Category-wise adjusted win rates of Sabiá-2 Medium against proprietary models on BRACEval, with 0.5 as the decisive threshold: below, Sabiá-2 excels; above, competitor models are superior. The green sub-circle shows categories where Sabiá-2 Medium outperforms. Sabiá-2 Medium surpasses all models in the harmful category, winning across all questions against most competitors. Conversely, the model exhibits weakness in math and coding.
